items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: my uncle and my father came to the house... Uncle Jim said this particular day... I didn't see my uncle for another three or four weeks... grateful to, it's my Uncle Jim for, I guess, spurring me on like that to play.

ctx.x: But the most significant thing about that was that just before my thirteenth birthday... As I said before, my birthday is September 6, and I think it was in August, about the middle of August... That's just before my thirteenth birthday. My uncle and my father came to the house with a truck. It was a truck that my uncle used on his job. He worked at a used furniture store, and I guess the guy that had the store used to go buy used furniture and sell it to the Blacks in the ghetto there. Anyway, my father came in…

Anyway, they unloaded the piano and brought it into the house and sat it in the living room. My uncle, who used to... We were always glad to see him because he was always giving us anything from pennies to nickels to dimes or whatever, and we were always glad to see Uncle Jim. Uncle Jim said this particular day, after he sat down at the piano, "Okay. The first one of you kids that learns to play something on this piano, I'm going to give 'em five dollars." Wow, that was a whole lot of money, because then it was…
